presentingComplaint: Documented fever for 5 weeks with fatigue and 4 kg weight loss, referred as query 'diabetic infection vs cancer recurrence'.
history: Type 2 diabetes for 18 years (HbA1c 8.4%) and breast carcinoma treated 4 years ago (currently in remission on annual surveillance). For 5 weeks she has had daily fevers to 38.5-38.8 C, worse in the late afternoon, with drenching night sweats, anorexia and 4 kg unintentional weight loss. Two prior primary-care courses of empirical antibiotics (co-amoxiclav then nitrofuranitoin for presumed UTI) produced no response. Comorbidities repeatedly anchored the picture: fever was first attributed to a diabetic foot/urinary focus, then to suspected breast-cancer relapse. However, a complete first-pass inpatient work-up has been unrevealing: three sets of blood cultures negative, urine culture sterile, chest radiograph and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis show no abscess, no lymph-node mass and no recurrent tumour, and mammography/tumour-marker surveillance are stable. No localising symptoms, no cough, no dysuria, no joint swelling. No recent travel; lives in an urban area; no TB contact known; no IVDU. She thus fulfils classic PUO criteria (fever >38.3 C, >3 weeks, undiagnosed after appropriate initial inpatient investigation), with two major comorbidities confounding early triage.
examination: Frail, mildly cachectic elderly woman, alert and not toxic. No rash, no eschar, no stigmata of endocarditis, no new murmur. Chest clear. Abdomen soft; spleen tip just palpable; no hepatomegaly, no focal tenderness. Small mobile 1 cm cervical and axillary nodes. Diabetic feet intact, no ulcer. Temporal arteries non-tender, no scalp tenderness or jaw claudication reported. No synovitis.
imaging: CXR normal. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: no abscess, no dominant lymphadenopathy, no organomegaly beyond a marginally enlarged spleen, no recurrent breast malignancy. No focal source identified on first-pass cross-sectional imaging.
microbiology: Three sets of blood cultures negative; urine sterile; procalcitonin low; HIV non-reactive. No microbiological source identified after initial appropriate work-up.
finalDiagnosis: Pyrexia (fever) of unknown origin - classic PUO fulfilling criteria after unrevealing initial inpatient work-up, with diabetes and prior malignancy as confounding comorbidities
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Fever of Unknown Origin (2022)
IDSA - Diagnostic Approach to Fever of Unknown Origin (2022)
stewardship: Classic PUO in a haemodynamically stable, non-neutropenic, non-toxic patient: empirical antibiotics are NOT indicated and should be withheld, as they obscure the diagnosis (e.g. partially treat endocarditis, delay TB/lymphoma diagnosis) and drive resistance - two prior empirical courses already failed. Pursue a structured second-tier work-up before any antimicrobial. Reserve empirical therapy (Access-tier, e.g. IV ceftriaxone) only if she develops sepsis/haemodynamic instability or a source is confirmed. Avoid empirical corticosteroids until GCA/lymphoma are excluded.
contraindications: Do not start empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics in a stable classic PUO
Do not give empirical corticosteroids before excluding lymphoma and confirming GCA
Avoid anchoring on diabetes/prior malignancy and stopping the systematic work-up
edgeCases: Diabetes and prior breast cancer bias clinicians toward diabetic infection or relapse, delaying the true diagnosis
Low procalcitonin with high ESR/CRP argues against occult bacterial sepsis and toward TB, malignancy or vasculitis
Elderly patient: GCA can present as isolated fever without headache and must be actively excluded
expectedMaiK: Recognise this fulfils classic PUO criteria; continue a structured, escalating diagnostic work-up (directed by potentially diagnostic clues) and WITHHOLD empirical antibiotics and steroids while haemodynamically stable.

Any headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication or visual symptoms (GCA)?
Detailed drug, travel, animal and occupational exposure history?
Any localising symptom or new lymph-node/mass since onset?
expectedInvestigations: Repeat/extended blood cultures (prolonged incubation) and echocardiography for culture-negative endocarditis
Peripheral smear, LDH, protein electrophoresis and excision biopsy of an accessible lymph node
Temporal artery biopsy / large-vessel imaging given age and very high ESR
FDG-PET/CT to localise occult infection, malignancy or large-vessel vasculitis
Interferon-gamma release assay, sputum/tissue AFB and mycobacterial cultures

Engine must NOT recommend empirical antibiotics for a stable classic PUO (antibiotics list empty)
